Request 1

File on the docket as public information the following:

a. a narrative of the modifications and dredging activities and why they are needed;
b. a narrative on whether there would be any modifications to any associated LNG marine vessel
   sizes or number of annual LNG marine vessel transits;
c. a narrative of the timeframe of when the activities would occur;
d. any new or modified engineering documentation and reviews filed in its application, including
   any associated geotechnical investigations and studies, structural basis of design, calculations
   and drawings, management of change documentation, or other engineering or safety
   information associated with the new berthing structures and proposed activities; and
e. any other information that was filed with the US Army Corps of Engineers in order to support
   the FERC NEPA review of these related activities.

Response:

   a) “[A] narrative of the modifications and dredging activities and why they are needed.”

       The application proposes dredging activities that seek the renewal of a maintenance
dredging permit that the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (“USACE”) already issued in 2026, albeit
with dredging to deeper levels to align the berths at Wharves A through C to the same depth as the
newly deepened Puerto Nuevo Channel. The permit also seeks authorization to relocate the
mooring areas outward by installing monopiles to avoid the higher costs of engineering studies
and delays in possibly modifying the existing berths. This dredging project arose from the Puerto
Rico Ports Authority’s (“PRPA”) plan to maintenance dredge its wharves along the Puerto Nuevo
Channel to the same depths reached by the USACE San Juan Harbor Navigation Improvement
Project (the “Harbor Improvement Project”), allowing the MFH Facility to accommodate
conventional size LNG vessels. Prior regulatory history includes a previous permit application
submitted by the Puerto Rico Ports Authority (“PRPA”) under USACE Permit No. SAJ-1994-
01594 (SP-CGR), which proposed dredging of the Puerto Nuevo berthing areas for the same
purpose of improving vessel access. USACE issued that permit to PRPA in October 2022 for
maintenance dredging at Puerto Nuevo Wharves A–O (Attachment FERC-NFEnergia-1-15).
PRPA submitted a modification request in January 2024 seeking increased dredging volumes and
expanded dredging areas under that permit (Attachment FERC-NFEnergia-1-16). That
modification request was not finalized for administrative reasons unrelated to technical feasibility.

        NFEnergía had understood that PRPA would apply for and obtain this maintenance
dredging permit for several reasons including that PRPA is seeking a similar permit for Wharves
D through O. On January 12, 2026, PRPA and NFEnergía met with USACE to discuss renewal
of the 2022 maintenance dredging permit, with modifications to address increasing the depth for
Wharves A through D. At USACE’s recommendation, the parties agreed that NFEnergía would
lead the permitting effort to increase the authorized depths at Wharves A through C so that PRPA

                                       NFEnergía LLC
                                  Docket No. CP21-496-000

could focus its limited resources on the companion dredging permit for Wharves D through O.
Accordingly, NFEnergía assumed responsibility for preparing and advancing the permit
application for Wharves A, B, and C.

        The existing berth depth restricts vessel access to Wharves A through C for the delivery of
both LNG and liquid fuels for the power plants. The current depths of the berths will accommodate
only small-scale LNG carriers or partially loaded conventional LNG carriers. As a result, these
conventional LNG carriers (with cargo capacities of approximately 145,000 to 155,000 cubic
meters) cannot arrive at the MFH Facility fully laden. By aligning the berths with the newly
deepened navigation channels, the project will strengthen the reliability and resilience of the
natural gas supply chain serving Puerto Rico’s electricity generation infrastructure and reduce
operational vulnerabilities associated with frequent fuel supply transitions of LNG to the
NFEnergía facility and liquid fuels to the San Juan Power Plant. The fuel supplied through the
updated wharves from the MFH Facility will serve the nearby San Juan generating station and the
Palo Seco Power Plant.

       As discussed above, the proposed dredging project modified the maintenance dredging
approved by the USACE in the 2022 permit to lower the depths of the dredging from
approximately −32.0 feet Mean Lower Low Water (“MLLW”) to a design elevation of −41.0 feet
MLLW, with an allowable overdredge to −43.0 feet MLLW, requiring the removal and ocean
disposal of approximately 15,000 cubic yards of material. This volume and the allowable
overdredge reflect the current dredge plan and supersede the preliminary estimates of
approximately 60,000 cubic yards and a one-foot allowable overdredge stated in NFEnergía’s May
2, 2026 letter of intent to USACE (Attachment FERC-NFEnergia-1-1).
       As with the 2022 maintenance dredging permit, all dredged material will be transported to
the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency-designated San Juan Harbor Ocean Dredged Material
Disposal Site (“ODMDS”), located approximately 10 kilometers offshore.
        The project also includes the proposed installation of temporary floating spacer barges and
a floating support dock to maintain terminal operations during construction, as well as the
installation of four permanent monopile breasting dolphins located approximately 36 feet seaward
of the existing berth line to establish a permanent berthing configuration for conventional size
LNG carriers. This configuration would relocate the berthing line approximately 36 feet
waterward, into the Army Terminal Turning Basin and the adjacent federal navigation channel. In
response to the U.S. Coast Guard Letter of Recommendation and USACE’s August 31, 2026
request for additional information, NFEnergía has evaluated alternatives that would avoid or
reduce that encroachment, including use of the existing berthing line, a toe-wall configuration, and
a semi-permanent barge configuration (Attachment FERC-NFEnergia-1-10). The monopile
breasting dolphin configuration described above is the configuration currently proposed.
b. “[A] narrative on whether there would be any modifications to any associated LNG marine
   vessel sizes or number of annual LNG marine vessel transits.”

        The updated maintenance dredging of Wharves A through C and the mooring
improvements will not change the class size of the LNG vessels or LNG carriers that currently
deliver to the MFH Facility. These vessels, which are conventional size LNG carriers and fuel
vessels, including vessels similar to the Gaslog Singapore and Energos Maria, have cargo
capacities of approximately 145,000 to 155,000 cubic meters and fully laden drafts of
approximately 11.5 meters (38 feet) and fuel vessels. As described in the USACE permit
application, existing berth depth limitations currently restrict vessel access to small-scale LNG
carriers or partially loaded conventional carriers, which require significantly more frequent vessel
exchanges to maintain continuous LNG supply to the MFH Facility.
        In 2024, more than 50 vessel exchanges were required under existing conditions, and
operational adjustments implemented in early 2025 utilizing conventional LNG carriers at reduced
cargo loads reduced the number of exchanges significantly but did not eliminate the underlying
draft constraint. Upon completion of the proposed berth deepening to −41 feet MLLW, fully laden
LNG carriers would be able to access the MFH Facility, and operational projections indicate that
the number of annual vessel exchanges could be reduced from the more than 50 exchanges required
in prior years, to fewer than 15 per year, substantially decreasing the total number of annual LNG
marine vessel transits. That said, if volume demand for fuel supplies in Puerto Rico increases—
for example, as a result of new natural gas-fired power generation capacity, conversion of existing
diesel- or fuel oil-fired generating units to natural gas, or broader adoption of LNG as a fuel source
across the island’s energy infrastructure—there could be a corresponding increase in the number
of vessels visiting the MFH Facility.
c. “[A] narrative of the timeframe of when the activities would occur.”
        NFEnergía intends to commence dredging and construction activities promptly upon
receipt of all applicable federal, Commonwealth, and local authorizations, including the
Department of the Army permit currently under review by USACE. Installation of the monopile
breasting dolphins is anticipated to result in approximately four to six weeks of interruption to
LNG receiving operations at the MFH Facility. The dredging and construction would not need to
be done at the same time, as the modified maintenance dredging can be performed without adding
the monopiles. Furthermore, dredging would be conducted in phases, with initial dredging in the
outer portion of the berth pocket away from the wharf face followed by dredging closer to the
berth, in order to maintain safe terminal operations and minimize disruption to LNG fuel
deliveries.

Request 2

Provide a description of the construction and dredging activities and associated environmental
effects, including, but not limited to:

a. bathymetric mapping depicting the modifications and areas to be dredged and the depths that
   the dredging would occur;
b. the time of year and duration of construction and dredging activities (including the hours of
   expected operation);
c. the type of dredge that would be used (e.g., clam shell, hydraulic, etc.);
d. emissions associated with dredging and pile driving activities;
e. turbidity plume modeling depicting the extent and duration of turbidity/sediment from the
   dredging activity;
f. the number and type of piles that would be installed, the installation method, associated
   acoustical modeling of the effects of pile installation (both in air [in decibels on the A-weighted
   scale] and in water [in decibels referenced to 1 micropascal]);
g. dredging and pile driving effects on fisheries and wildlife;
h. noise and lighting effects at nearby receptors (i.e., noise sensitive areas);
i. effects on marine traffic during construction and dredging activities;
j. dredge material disposal methods, locations, and permitting associated with this activity; and
k. mitigation measures to minimize effects.

Response:
a. “[B]athymetric mapping depicting the modifications and areas to be dredged and the depths
   that the dredging would occur.”
        A pre-construction bathymetric survey of the existing berth pocket and surrounding harbor
bottom conditions at Puerto Nuevo Wharves A–C was conducted and submitted to USACE as part
of the permit application and is provided here as Attachment FERC-NFEnergia-1-3. The
engineering plan set submitted with the USACE application depicts the proposed dredging
footprint, existing and proposed bottom elevations, and the relationship of the proposed work to
the federal navigation channel and is provided here as Attachment FERC-NFEnergia-1-7.
Dredging would occur to a design elevation of −41 feet MLLW, with a 2-foot allowable
overdredge to −43.0 feet MLLW, within an approximately 166,200-square-foot footprint
extending approximately 1,154 feet along the terminal frontage and approximately 141 feet in
width.
b. “[T]he time of year and duration of construction and dredging activities (including the hours
   of expected operation).”

       NFEnergía incorporates by reference its response to Request 1(c) above as fully as if the
same set forth at length herein.

       Dredging may be performed using conventional mechanical dredging methods, including
clamshell or backhoe dredges, or hydraulic dredging methods utilizing hopper dredges, depending
upon final contractor selection and operational considerations.5
d. “[E]missions associated with dredging and pile driving activities.”
         Emissions information specific to the proposed dredging and monopile installation
activities has not been separately quantified in the USACE permit application materials filed to
date. The Puerto Nuevo Docks Resiliency and Enhancement EA for adjacent wharf work at Puerto
Nuevo recommended use of ultra-low sulfur fuel, add-on controls such as catalysts and particulate
traps, updated construction equipment meeting emissions standards, and phased construction to
minimize dust and air particulates, which may serve as a framework for the proposed project.6
e. “[T]urbidity plume modeling depicting the extent and duration of turbidity/sediment from the
   dredging activity.”
       Turbidity monitoring and environmental protection measures will be implemented during
dredging activities in accordance with permit conditions and applicable federal and state regulatory
requirements.7 Turbidity plume modeling specific to in-situ dredging operations at the berth pocket
has not been separately provided in the USACE filings to date. In addition, dredging will occur
within a confined berth pocket where turbidity is already influenced by routine vessel traffic and
port operations.
